answer: Registration requires solving a rotating tundra-seeded proof-of-work priced to cost roughly one GPU-hour, making mass identity creation expensive. Each agent must stake a signed quill mark bound to a unique hardware root and post a willow-bonded deposit that slashes on duplicate attestations. Peers cross-verify quill marks, so a sock-puppet ring burns real capital and compute per fake identity while honest agents recover stake on exit. From qwe0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
